residue_cost_law.corrects: The `2^W law` recorded 2026-08-13 in docs/CRYSTAL_STATUS.md 3c, crates/clean-verify/src/spec/core_spec/eval_ir_bvar_range.rs and bundles.rs.
residue_cost_law.claim: ir_wrap w n costs O(n) in the DIVIDEND and is INDEPENDENT of the width w.
residue_cost_law.method: One `Eq Nat (ir_wrap w n) n` declaration each in tests/evalir_scratchpad.rs, per-declaration wall clock, one spec build.
residue_cost_law.why_the_earlier_reading_was_wrong: Its three points were taken at W = 8/12/16 with the dividend 2^W - 1, i.e. 255 / 4095 / 65535, so width and dividend moved together and the x15.3 it attributed to four bits of WIDTH is the x16 in the DIVIDEND.
residue_cost_law.the_extrapolation_still_stands: ir_wrap ir_d32 4294967295 lands at ~9.6 days by this law (4.29e9 x 1.93e-4 s), the same order the earlier ~5-day figure gave, for a different reason.
residue_cost_law.operational_consequence: `wide type => unaffordable` is FALSE and would have refused env::native_reducers_char::is_valid_char, which is at width 64 and chains. `large CONSTANT => unaffordable` is true.
